title: Nepal Army: over 300 rescued as two hydropower tunnels stay cut off
body: The Nepali Army says its units have rescued more than 300 people across the flood zone so far, spokesperson Brigadier General Raja Ram Basnet said, a wider tally than NDRRMA's earlier, named count of 113. Around two dozen helicopters and nearly 1,000 personnel from the Nepal Police, Nepali Army and Armed Police Force are working the search, the Kathmandu Post reports.

Two hydropower tunnels are still cut off. At Trishuli 3A in Mailung, 35 workers are cut off with the tunnel gate blocked, according to messages one worker sent his wife on Wednesday afternoon before contact was lost. There has been no rescue update there since, the Kathmandu Post reports.

At the Langtang Hydropower project, more than 25 workers have been out of contact in a tunnel since Wednesday. Bijay Mohan Bhattarai, the company's managing director and a secretary of IPPAN, said government agencies need to step up rescue efforts there, and that all available helicopters had already been sent elsewhere, Onlinekhabar reports.

The Independent Power Producers' Association Nepal, IPPAN, says 215 staff from five hydropower projects in total have not been reached since Wednesday's flood. Worst hit is the under construction Upper Trishuli-1 project, with 94 people out of contact. At Rasuwagadhi, 51 staff are out of contact, though 3 reached higher ground on their own.
